full_name: Variance-Reduced Mirror Descent for Smooth Convex Finite-Sum Optimization
source_reference: Lan, First-order and Stochastic Optimization Methods for Machine Learning, Springer 2020 (Corollary 5.8)

problem.description: Composite finite-sum convex optimization over a closed convex set

variable_space.math: X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m \text{ closed convex}; \; f(x) = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m} f_i(x); \; h : X \to \mathbb{R} \text{ simple convex (possibly nondifferentiable)}

assumptions.name: Component smoothness
assumptions.math: \|\nabla f_i(x) - \nabla f_i(y)\|_* \le L_i \|x - y\|, \quad \forall x, y \in X, \; i = 1, \ldots, m

assumptions.name: Component convexity
assumptions.math: f_i \text{ is convex on } X, \quad \forall i = 1, \ldots, m
assumptions.ref: Section 5.3, p.279 (prose preceding Eq. 5.3.1): 'f is the average of m smooth convex component functions f_i'
assumptions._origin_correction: Initial JSON extraction captured only displayed-math assumptions; this prose-stated component convexity (page 279, in the setup paragraph immediately preceding Eq. 5.3.1) was missed. Verified against PDF Section 5.3 setup paragraph. Used in Lemma 5.12 proof (page 280): 'By Lemma 5.8 (with f = f_i)' --- Lemma 5.8 is co-coercivity, mathematically requiring f_i convex.

assumptions.name: Convexity of f
assumptions.math: f(y) \ge f(x) + \langle \nabla f(x), y - x \rangle, \quad \forall x, y \in X

assumptions.name: Sampling distribution
assumptions.math: Q = \{q_1, \ldots, q_m\} \text{ probability distribution on } \{1, \ldots, m\}; \quad L_Q := \frac{1}{m} \max_{i=1,\ldots,m} \frac{L_i}{q_i}

assumptions.name: Distance generating function
assumptions.math: v : X \to \mathbb{R} \text{ continuously differentiable, 1-strongly convex w.r.t. } \|\cdot\|; \quad V(x, z) = v(z) - [v(x) + \langle \nabla v(x), z - x \rangle]

steps.name: Epoch setup
steps.math: \tilde{x} = \tilde{x}^{s-1}, \; \tilde{g} = \nabla f(\tilde{x}), \; x_1 = x^{s-1}, \; T = T_s, \; Q = \{q_1, \ldots, q_m\} \text{ on } \{1, \ldots, m\}

steps.name: Variance-reduced gradient estimator
steps.math: \text{Pick } i_t \in \{1, \ldots, m\} \text{ randomly according to } Q; \quad G_t = \frac{\nabla f_{i_t}(x_t) - \nabla f_{i_t}(\tilde{x})}{q_{i_t} m} + \tilde{g}

steps.name: Mirror descent prox update
steps.math: x_{t+1} = \operatorname{argmin}_{x \in X} \left\{ \gamma [\langle G_t, x \rangle + h(x)] + V(x_t, x) \right\}

parameters.name: V
parameters.math: V(x, z) = v(z) - [v(x) + \langle \nabla v(x), z - x \rangle] \text{ (Bregman divergence)}

main_theorem.rate: \mathscr{O}\left\{ m \log \frac{\Psi(x^0) - \Psi(x^*) + L_Q V(x^0, x^*)}{\varepsilon} + \frac{\Psi(x^0) - \Psi(x^*) + L_Q V(x^0, x^*)}{\varepsilon} \right\}

proof.description: Sum the one-step expected recursion (5.3.11) with mu=0 over t=1,...,T inside one epoch and take expectation over i_1,...,i_T

For epoch s, set x_1 = x^{s-1}, \tilde{x} = \tilde{x}^{s-1}, x^s = x_{T_s+1}, and \tilde{x}^s = \sum_{t=2}^{T_s} x_t/(T_s - 1); use convexity of \Psi and 4L_Q\gamma \le 1 to obtain the epoch recursion
Sum the epoch inequalities over s=1,...,S using the definition of w_s, apply convexity of Psi on bar{x}^S, and use 4L_Q gamma <= 1

Substitute the Corollary 5.8 choices \theta=1, \gamma = 1/(16L_Q), and T_s = 2T_{s-1} with T_1 = 7; then w_s = \frac{1}{8} T_s - \frac{3}{4} \ge \frac{1}{56} T_s, so \sum_{s=1}^{S} w_s \ge \frac{1}{8}(2^S - 1), and combine this with \gamma(1 + 4L_Q\gamma T_1) = \frac{11}{64L_Q}
Count total gradient evaluations: each epoch s costs m + T_s component gradient evaluations; sum over S epochs to get the complexity bound (5.3.19)
proof.math: \mathscr{O}\left\{ m \log \frac{\Psi(x^0) - \Psi(x^*) + L_Q V(x^0, x^*)}{\varepsilon} + \frac{\Psi(x^0) - \Psi(x^*) + L_Q V(x^0, x^*)}{\varepsilon} \right\}

key_lemmas.name: Weighted component gradient-gap bound (Lemma 5.12)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m} \frac{1}{m q_i} \|\nabla f_i(x) - \nabla f_i(x^*)\|_*^2 \le 2 L_Q [\Psi(x) - \Psi(x^*)], \quad \forall x \in X

proof.description: Use optimality of x* for Psi and convexity of h to replace -<nabla f(x*), x - x*> by the h-gap
proof.math: f(x) - f(x^*) - \langle \nabla f(x^*), x - x^* \rangle \le f(x) - f(x^*) + h(x) - h(x^*) = \Psi(x) - \Psi(x^*)

key_lemmas.name: Variance bound for VR estimator (Lemma 5.13)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Conditionally on } x_1, \ldots, x_t: \quad \mathbb{E}[\delta_t] = 0, \quad \mathbb{E}[\|\delta_t\|_*^2] \le 2 L_Q [f(\tilde{x}) - f(x_t) - \langle \nabla f(x_t), \tilde{x} - x_t \rangle], \quad \mathbb{E}[\|\delta_t\|_*^2] \le 4 L_Q [\Psi(x_t) - \Psi(x^*) + \Psi(\tilde{x}) - \Psi(x^*)]

key_lemmas.name: Two-center Bregman prox inequality (Lemma 3.5)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let } p : X \to \mathbb{R} \text{ be convex, } \tilde{x}, \tilde{y} \in X, \; \mu_1, \mu_2 \ge 0. \text{ If } \hat{u} \in \operatorname{Argmin}\{p(u) + \mu_1 V(\tilde{x}, u) + \mu_2 V(\tilde{y}, u) : u \in X\}, \text{ then } p(\hat{u}) + \mu_1 V(\tilde{x}, \hat{u}) + \mu_2 V(\tilde{y}, \hat{u}) \le p(u) + \mu_1 V(\tilde{x}, u) + \mu_2 V(\tilde{y}, u) - (\mu_1 + \mu_2) V(\hat{u}, u), \; \forall u \in X
key_lemmas.role: Provides the general Bregman prox inequality used in the one-step analysis of the mirror descent update in Lemma 5.14

proof.description: Write the first-order optimality condition for the minimizer hat{u}
proof.math: \langle p'(\hat{u}) + \mu_1 \nabla V(\tilde{x}, \hat{u}) + \mu_2 \nabla V(\tilde{y}, \hat{u}), u - \hat{u} \rangle \ge 0, \quad \forall u \in X

proof.description: Use the Bregman three-point identity V(tilde{x}, u) = V(tilde{x}, hat{u}) + <nabla V(tilde{x}, hat{u}), u - hat{u}> + V(hat{u}, u) and convexity of p to derive the inequality
proof.math: p(\hat{u}) + \mu_1 V(\tilde{x}, \hat{u}) + \mu_2 V(\tilde{y}, \hat{u}) \le p(u) + \mu_1 V(\tilde{x}, u) + \mu_2 V(\tilde{y}, u) - (\mu_1 + \mu_2) V(\hat{u}, u)

key_lemmas.name: One-step VRMD progress bound (Lemma 5.14)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{If } L\gamma \le 1/2, \text{ then } \forall x \in X: \quad \gamma [\Psi(x_{t+1}) - \Psi(x)] + V(x_{t+1}, x) \le (1 - \gamma \mu) V(x_t, x) + \gamma \langle \delta_t, x - x_t \rangle + \gamma^2 \|\delta_t\|_*^2. \quad \text{Moreover, conditionally on } i_1, \ldots, i_{t-1}: \quad \gamma \mathbb{E}[\Psi(x_{t+1}) - \Psi(x^*)] + \mathbb{E}[V(x_{t+1}, x^*)] \le (1 - \gamma \mu) V(x_t, x^*) + 4 L_Q \gamma^2 [\Psi(x_t) - \Psi(x^*) + \Psi(\tilde{x}) - \Psi(x^*)]
key_lemmas.role: Provides the per-step descent recursion that is summed over epochs to yield the convergence bound

proof.description: Use smoothness of f with L*gamma <= 1/2 to upper-bound gamma*f(x_{t+1}) by a linearization plus the quadratic error term gamma^2 ||delta_t||^2_*
proof.math: \gamma f(x_{t+1}) \le \gamma [f(x_t) + \langle G_t, x_{t+1} - x_t \rangle] + V(x_t, x_{t+1}) + \gamma^2 \|\delta_t\|_*^2

proof.description: Apply Lemma 3.5 to the prox update defining x_{t+1} and combine with convexity of f to obtain (5.3.10)
proof.math: \gamma [\Psi(x_{t+1}) - \Psi(x)] + V(x_{t+1}, x) \le (1 - \gamma \mu) V(x_t, x) + \gamma \langle \delta_t, x - x_t \rangle + \gamma^2 \|\delta_t\|_*^2

proof.description: Set x = x*, take conditional expectation, use E[delta_t] = 0, and apply the variance bound (5.3.8) from Lemma 5.13 to obtain (5.3.11)

key_lemmas.name: Epoch-averaged bound (Theorem 5.6)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Suppose } \theta_t = 1, \; 4 L_Q \gamma \le 1, \; w_s := (1 - 4 L_Q \gamma)(T_{s-1} - 1) - 4 L_Q \gamma T_s > 0. \text{ Then } \mathbb{E}[\Psi(\bar{x}^S) - \Psi(x^*)] \le \frac{\gamma (1 + 4 L_Q \gamma T_1)[\Psi(x^0) - \Psi(x^*)] + V(x^0, x^*)}{\gamma \sum_{s=1}^{S} w_s}
key_lemmas.role: Provides the multi-epoch convergence bound for the smooth (mu=0) case by telescoping the one-step recursion, directly yielding Corollary 5.8 after parameter substitution

proof.description: For epoch s, sum Eq. (5.3.11) with mu=0 over t=1,...,T_s, take expectation, and use convexity of Psi together with 4L_Q\gamma \le 1 to replace the inner-iterate average by \tilde{x}^s
Telescope the epoch recursion over s=1,...,S, use the definition of w_s and nonnegativity of V, and apply convexity of Psi on bar{x}^S
